scope: All 1,260 saved outputs counted; 12 deliberately selected examples inspected; 84 answers for seven questions source-reviewed. This is targeted diagnosis, not a random manual accuracy estimate.

findings.text: Native-call notes helped 7 and harmed 20 Thinking answers across 210 trials after targeted score corrections.
One recovered microphone answer accounts for about 60 percent of the net thinking-token saving; the median trial uses 15.5 more tokens.
Accepted note edits can overwrite correct evidence, add false certainty or distract the answer from facts still present in the transcript.
The next test removes generated note text while retaining the same selected source passages.

examples.title: A design suggestion became a claim of implementation readiness.
examples.question: Assistant, what's the current status on the speech recognition implementation? I need to know if it's ready for the interface.
examples.reference: The team discussed mapping speech commands to functions already present. The available discussion does not report a finished implementation or demonstrate that it is ready for interface integration.

reactive.answer: The transcript doesn't provide a clear status on whether speech recognition implementation is ready. D mentions they 'covered that with our screen and speech recognition' and don't expect it to be a problem. B expresses uncertainty about implementation: 'I'm not sure how to implement it into the remote control.' A states, 'I don't think you have to design anything else for that,' suggesting it's already settled but not explicitly confirmed as ready.

with_notes.answer: Speech recognition implementation is ready for the interface. A confirmed no new design is needed as speech commands can be matched with existing functions (TS3006c-U00260, TS3006c-U00263). B asked if speech would be for basic options only or for everything, but A's confirmation means it's ready to use with current interface.

notes.fact: B raised uncertainty about how to implement speech recognition into the remote control design. A suggested matching speech commands with existing functions, and A confirmed no new design is needed for speech recognition.

examples.observation: The reactive Thinking call reaches 16,384 thinking tokens without a final answer. With native-call notes it answers microphone using 897 thinking tokens. examples.title: Agreement remains a difficult scoring boundary.
examples.question: Assistant, was it agreed that the remote should control only TV or also connected devices like DVD players?
examples.reference: TV plus connected devices such as DVD players was the initial desired scope. A then proposed a TV-only backup, and C tentatively suggested concentrating on a good TV remote. The available discussion does not settle one final scope.

reactive.answer: The group discussed controlling TV and connected devices (e.g., DVD players) but also considered a TV-only backup due to cost. No final agreement was reached; they plan to finalize in the next meeting.

examples.observation: C describes desired multi-device functions while a later fallback remains conditional on cost. The scope of group agreement needs additional source adjudication before using this case to explain an answer-quality gain.

examples.title: The transcript supports an attribution absent from the short key.
examples.question: Assistant, can you clarify how the functional and conceptual design phases differ in terms of deliverables?
examples.reference: Functional design specifies required functions and tasks; conceptual design covers how people use the remote. Initial component identification may already begin during functional design.

reactive.answer: Functional design specifies required functions (e.g., what the remote must do), while conceptual design focuses on user interaction and interface (e.g., how users will use it), as explained by C during the meeting.

with_notes.answer: Functional design focuses on required functions and specific capabilities (what the remote control needs to do), while conceptual design focuses on how the remote control will be structured and presented, including user interaction (how it will be done).
